name: Trackaholic
description: A full-stack, multi-user nutrition tracking app: a React + TypeScript PWA backed by a FastAPI + SQLAlchemy REST API on PostgreSQL, with AI meal analysis that shows its uncertainty.

paragraphs: Formerly Macros Calculator; renamed in October 2026, and moved from macros-calculator-mu.vercel.app to trackaholic.app the same month.
🔗 Live app: trackaholic.app — sign up and start logging. (Free-tier hosting: the first request after idle can take 30–60 s.)
A full-stack, multi-user nutrition tracking app: a React + TypeScript dashboard UI (installable as a PWA) backed by a FastAPI + SQLAlchemy REST API on PostgreSQL.
features: Email + password auth: Argon2id password hashing, JWT bearer tokens (7-day expiry), per-IP rate limiting on login, signup and password reset

Per-user everything: meals, food library, saved meal templates, weight entries, water logs, step counts, supplements and their check-offs, calorie plans, goals/settings, and AI analyses are isolated per account —…

Layered AI quotas: 12 analyses + 16 voice notes + 3 review summaries per user per day, under a global ceiling of 40 calls/day across every account — sized for Gemini's free tier of 20 requests a day per model, and…

What the AI sees: your photos, voice note and description are sent to Google Gemini to estimate the meal, and the app says so under the Estimate button. Photos are shrunk on your phone first, which also strips their…

What you search for is not logged: the food searches send what you type as a URL parameter, and both the server's access log and its outgoing-request log blank that value before writing the line. The app's own log lines…
